structured_output.what_is_happening: DDOS ("Degens Dollars On Solana") is a pump.fun coin created about 17 minutes before collection. It left the bonding curve and moved to PumpSwap about 4 minutes after creation. Its only social link is a Polymarket X post, which suggests it is riding a viral Polymarket tweet that used the phrase or a DDoS-style joke. About $370k of volume went through in roughly 12 minutes, from 1,356 unique buyers. It peaked around $171k market cap and has since fallen to about $109k, with a 5-minute move of -17% to -27%. At least 10 copycats with the same name exist. This is the largest and most liquid of the live ones.

narrative.description: A meme riding a Polymarket X post, a fast 'tweet coin' play. The fee-redirect note ('Fees to @usepaid') and a CTO-style profile suggest the post was hijacked rather than coming from a real project.
narrative.why_spreading: A big-brand tweet (Polymarket) prompted many degen deployments at once. The first deployment to reach PumpSwap draws the most flow. Whether it keeps going depends on the tweet staying relevant and on whether Polymarket or KOLs acknowledge the token.

token_connection.why_this_token: Among the live same-name tokens it has the highest market cap and most holders, and it was one of the first to migrate (pair created 1790387138). That points to it being the leading copy by flow. Nothing links it officially to Polymarket.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 10 same-name DDOS tokens were created within minutes. Several have $20-31k liquidity and large hourly volume (FDT6… $250k, 9zMg… $176k, E2t6… $166k). One (26BU…) was earlier but its liquidity has been drained.

authenticity.evidence: Buyer breadth looks real: 1,356 unique buyers, 1,765 holders, and the largest single holder has only about 3%. Against that, GMGN tags 418 bundler wallets, puts the bot/degen rate at 70%, and says the top bundler traders hold 33%. The creator has closed out, and 4 insiders sit in a transfer network. There are no paid boosts. It is flagged as a community takeover.
authenticity.uncertainty: No X data, so I cannot tell how far the Polymarket tweet itself is spreading. Bundler tags on tweet-coin launches often just catch copy-trading bots.

structural_risks: Heavy bundler/bot participation (33% held by top bundler traders) makes a sharp coordinated dump likely
Price is already about 36% below the ATH and falling on the 5-minute window at entry
Ten or more copycats split attention and liquidity
Only about $24-29k of liquidity against more than $100k of market cap

structured_output.counterargument: Leading coins on tweets from big accounts like Polymarket can run to seven figures if the tweet goes viral or Polymarket acknowledges it. Holders are unusually spread out, mint, freeze and LP are all clean, and this is the clear flow leader among the copies. The dip at entry could be a healthy pullback before a second leg.
unknowns: What the Polymarket post actually says and how viral it is
Whether Polymarket or major KOLs will endorse any DDOS token
Whether bundler wallets will exit together
Whether a competing copy takes over the 'canonical' status

source_coverage.notes: No internet in this condition; judged from the packet only.

structured_output.thesis: A brand-tweet meme with real breadth. It is the leader among many copycats, but it is already fading from its ATH, bundler share is high and the creator has exited. It has a better-than-average tail chance because of the attention level and the Polymarket link. The most likely path is chop or a fade as the copycats and bots split the flow.
